test_policy.notes: SAT/ACT are not required for admission. The Common Data Set says scores are optional, used case by case to enhance the academic profile, and not required for scholarship consideration.

requirements.notes: International applicants use NAU's international application: $50 undergraduate fee (the domestic fee is $40), official transcripts (certified translation if not in English), passport copy, English proficiency and proof of financial support for the I-20. Minimum 2.5 GPA for the last 3 years of secondary school. The enrollment fee for first-year undergraduates is $325. No essay or recommendation is listed.

deadlines.label: Priority admission, fall 2027 (international)
deadlines.notes: NAU accepts international undergraduate applications year-round; applying by the priority date gives an earlier decision, access to the housing application and more time for the I-20 and visa. Spring priority is Sept. 15. NAU recommends applying 4-6 months before the start date.

deadlines.label: Application closing date, fall (CDS)
deadlines.notes: The Common Data Set gives Aug. 1 (no year printed) as the application closing date and says decisions are sent on a rolling basis. The international pages publish no hard deadline other than the priority dates.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Other accepted proof: ACT English and Reading 21+, SAT EBRW 350+, IB English A (5 HL / 6 SL) or English B (7), transfer of one 3-credit English composition course, four years of English at a high school taught entirely in English (with school verification), exchange students with B2 English; citizens of English-speaking countries need no proof. Applicants below the minimum may enroll in the Program in Intensive English (PIE), with entry scores of Duolingo 55, IELTS 4 or TOEFL 20, until they meet NAU's requirement.

english.notes: TOEFL iBT and iBT Home Edition; MyBest score accepted.
The page lists '3.5 effective 1/21/2026' beside the 70 minimum (the new 1-6 scale).

aid.notes: International Excellence Award (IEA): up to $11,000 per year as an out-of-state tuition waiver for first-time, full-time F-1 undergraduates on the Flagstaff campus with a 3.0+ GPA at admission; no separate application, awarded first come, first served; renewable with full-time enrollment and a 3.0 GPA. Not available to sponsored students or dual-degree or PIE students. The Common Data Set says nonresidents get institutional non-need-based aid only. Foreign citizens are not eligible for FAFSA.
